commonProblems.h2: Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV combines proven EA888 Gen 3 petrol engine technology with a sophisticated hybrid system. While generally reliable, high-mileage examples can develop issues with the high-pressure fuel pump, hybrid battery degradation, and occasional hybrid control unit faults. The DGTA code dominates replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why the Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV DGTA Suffers from Fuel Delivery Issues
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) on EA888 Gen 3 engines can wear prematurely, causing metal debris to contaminate the fuel system and potentially damage injectors, leading to rough running, reduced power, and increased emissions.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: HPFP replacement and fuel system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for early-stage wear; prevents injector contamination if caught before metal debris spreads.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty, hybrid system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when HPFP failure has caused catastrophic injector damage or cylinder scoring.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV (2020-present) is worth ~£25,000-£45,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. A reconditioned or rebuilt engine is highly viable and justified by the warranty, as the replacement cost represents a sensible fraction of the vehicle's retained value ( Safe).
problems.recommendation: Address any HPFP warnings or unusual fuel system noises immediately. Preventative HPFP replacement is inexpensive compared to the labour required to rectify injector damage. If the engine block is already compromised, a full rebuild with hybrid system recalibration offers better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DGTA Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation - Why the Audi Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV Loses Electric Range Over Time
problems.rootCause: The 14.1kWh lithium-ion battery pack can degrade over time, especially with frequent fast charging or extreme temperature exposure, reducing electric-only range and potentially triggering hybrid system fault codes.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for partial degradation; restores some electric range without full pack replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty, hybrid system recalibration
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if battery degradation is compounded by engine mechanical failure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For Q5 55 TFSI e PHEV models worth £25,000+, a reconditioned engine justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. The hybrid battery is a separate component and should be assessed independently.
problems.recommendation: Monitor electric range regularly and have the battery health checked during routine servicing. If range has dropped significantly but the petrol engine is healthy, battery reconditioning may be more cost-effective than full engine replacement.
